currentContext.business: Sonata Software Limited (“SSL”) is primarily engaged in providing Information Technology Services and Solutions — IT consultancy, computer programming, modernization and testing support related activities — to customers in the United States of America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Australia and India. The Company describes itself as operating in two spheres: International IT Services and a Domestic products-and-services business run through its India arm Sonata Information Technology Limited (SITL), which expands the Microsoft channel, partners with other ISVs and pursues large System Integration deals. It is a public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office at Mumbai and operational headquarters at Bengaluru, and is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited.

currentContext.expansion: The routed text discloses no plant, capacity or physical capex programme — Sonata's expansion is asset-light and platform/capability-led. In FY26 the Company launched AgentBridge, its cloud-agnostic Agentic AI platform for building and deploying next-generation Agentic AI solutions, and operationalized it internally with production-grade agents running for the HR and Finance teams. Capability build-out continued through Sonata University, which trained more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers in AI and delivered organisation-wide Vibe Code training, and through Program Edge, under which internal workflows — including immigration management and compensation and benefits administration — are being automated with an AI layer on top. Ecosystem expansion took the form of research partnerships with IISc (India) and the Wharton School (US) on Agentic AI, and of deeper hyperscaler alliances: Microsoft (continuing Inner Circle and Partner AI Council member, among the first recognised as a Microsoft Frontier Partner, Official Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner) and AWS (Premier Tier Services Partner, Gen AI Competency Partner), alongside Salesforce and Snowflake. Market expansion is being pursued by scaling the invest verticals HLS and BFSI, by deepening the North America business, and in India (SITL) by expanding the Microsoft channel into the SMC segment, broadening ISV partnerships beyond the three hyperscaler CSPs, and winning large System Integration deals that integrate Cisco, IBM, Dell and other ISV infrastructures with leading cloud platforms. The workforce stood at 6200+ Sonatians.

risks.risk: Human capital development, retention and labour practices
risks.note: Flagged as a material risk in the BRSR: Sonata is a people-centric organisation and its sustained success is closely tied to its ability to attract, engage and retain highly skilled technology professionals; as the global shift toward digital transformation intensifies, the growing imbalance in skilled talent has become increasingly evident. Mitigation runs through engagement initiatives, the DNA (Deep Nurtured Attributes) core values and a rewards and recognition framework.

risks.risk: Privacy protection and cybersecurity / data breach exposure
risks.note: Flagged as a material risk in the BRSR: the expansion of operations along with increased adoption of remote working models may elevate the risk of data breaches; any failure to ensure data privacy or to report incidents in a timely manner could result in legal penalties, reputational damage with clients and potential financial exposure. Mitigated by certification audits for the Information Security Management Framework aligned with ISO 27001 and the Service Management Framework aligned with ISO 20000, plus security investments, access controls, threat monitoring and employee awareness training.

risks.risk: Climate change — climate risk, GHG emissions and possible carbon taxation
risks.note: Flagged as a material risk and opportunity in the BRSR: climate-related risks are increasingly impacting the operational environment and financial performance, and possible implementation of carbon taxation in the near term could influence the growth trajectory; transitioning to a low-carbon economy may require substantial upfront investment.

risks.risk: Corporate governance and business ethics / regulatory compliance burden
risks.note: Flagged as a material risk and opportunity in the BRSR: full legal compliance must be maintained and internal practices constantly updated to stay ahead of changing regulations; implementing high governance standards requires significant resources, described as a negative but mitigated financial impact and a vital investment for maintaining stakeholder confidence.

risks.risk: Dependence on the pace of client digital-transformation adoption
risks.note: Customer relationships are central to Sonata's business strategy and the growth of the customer base is closely aligned with the rate at which organisations adopt digital transformation initiatives — making revenue growth a function of external enterprise IT spending cycles.

risks.risk: Geographic revenue concentration in North America
risks.note: The North America business now represents over 74% of total revenue, up from approximately 54% three years ago, so demand or client conditions in a single market drive the bulk of the business; exports contribute 39% of the entity's total turnover.

The BRSR reports one business activity — Information Technology Services and Solutions (IT consultancy, computer programming, modernization, testing support) — at more than 90% of turnover, with computer programming, consultancy and related activities at 100% of turnover, leaving no diversification outside IT services.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the AI-led pivot
risks.note: Growth is concentrated in a set of explicit bets — AI-enabled services scaling to a stated share of revenue, large-deal pursuits, and the HLS and BFSI invest verticals — which depend on continued AI adoption by clients and on sustaining hyperscaler partner status (Microsoft Inner Circle/Frontier/Fabric, AWS Premier Tier and Gen AI Competency) rather than on a diversified base.

one-line thesis: Sonata delivered resilient Q4FY26 with 20.2% EBITDA margins driven by AI-enabled utilization (91.8%) despite flat international revenue, while domestic business stabilized post-OEM direct-billing shock. The appointment of Rajsekhar Datta Roy (30-year veteran/AI-architect) as CEO signals an aggressive pivot to monetize the $280M AI pipeline, targeting BFSI and TMT recovery in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs.2,536.2 Cr (Q4, -3.1% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 20.2% (Q4, +70bps QoQ); PAT: Rs.130.5 Cr (Q4, +21.4% YoY); Order Book: $95M (Q4, Book-to-Bill 1.16x); Net Debt: Net Cash Rs.31 Cr. One-offs: Domestic revenue degrowth (-25% QoQ) due to large client renewal loss to direct OEM billing; International USD revenue flattish (-2.1% YoY) offset by rupee depreciation.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Gradual improvement expected in FY27 led by BFSI/TMT; Margin: Maintain ~20% EBITDA (open to invest for growth); Order Inflow: Focus on converting $280M AI pipeline; Capex: No specific capex guidance, focusing on capability building and partnerships.
order book & pipeline: $95M total (Q4); AI-led portion $16.9M (Q4) / $49M (FY26), representing 18% of total book. Large deals: 2 won in Q4, 8 in FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: International: Revenue Rs.779.2 Cr (+5.5% QoQ), EBITDA 20.2%. Domestic: Revenue Rs.1,759.2 Cr (-25% QoQ, -8.3% YoY) due to channel disruption; PAT Rs.46.3 Cr (+3.9% QoQ).
growth verticals / optionality: $280M AI-led pipeline across 100+ clients; Harmoni.AI and AgentBridge differentiated offerings; Expansion in BFSI payments modernization and TMT upturn.
margins & cost dynamics: Margins accreted 70bps QoQ to 20.2% via utilization hike (91.8%), pyramid optimization, and price increases; offset partially by higher AI-led CSP bundle costs.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly quantified; strategy focuses on investing in workforce readiness (90% AI-trained), ecosystem partnerships, and differentiated IP rather than heavy infrastructure capex.
capital allocation: Net cash position of Rs.31 Cr; Final dividend recommended at Rs.4.15/share; M&A on hold for immediate future, evaluating only unique tech opportunities in medium term.
risks & watch-items: Elongated client decision cycles for AI projects; BFSI sector contraction pressures; Domestic channel policy changes by OEMs (Microsoft); Sustainability of TMT upturn.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; disciplined execution; focused on continuity during leadership transition; confident in AI pipeline conversion despite macro headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: AI-led orders now 18% of total book indicating rapid product mix shift; Domestic business already recovered most of the OEM direct-billing loss within 4 quarters despite reported degrowth; 90% of workforce already AI-certified creating a latent margin lever if utilization dips.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

business_model.body: Sonata Software Limited (“SSL”) is primarily engaged in providing Information Technology Services and Solutions — IT consultancy, computer programming, modernization and testing support related activities — to customers in the United States of America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Australia and India. The Company describes itself as operating in two spheres: International IT Services and a Domestic products-and-services business run through its India arm Sonata Information Technology Limited (SITL), which expands the Microsoft channel, partners with other ISVs and pursues large System Integration deals. It is a public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, with its registered office at Mumbai and operational headquarters at Bengaluru, and is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited.

- AI is moving from experimentation to industrial-scale adoption, and is becoming the operating layer of the modern enterprise rather than just a capability
- Enterprises are shifting from using technology as a tool for cost efficiency to viewing it as a core engine for commercial reinvention, moving beyond simple task automation toward augmented intelligence that creates new business models and revenue streams
- Organizations are moving beyond fragmented pilots to embedding AI across revenue, operations and engineering
- AI-led opportunities are scaling in the pipeline and are being pursued across 100+ clients, monetised through operational efficiency gains, faster time to market/customer experience, and transformation of business models
- FY26 was a year of resilience as the Company navigated headwinds from the market and from a few key clients; operations were strengthened structurally through technology-driven optimization, which management says reflected in growth and profit expansion
- Management intends to leverage Sonata's size and scale to deliver 'enterprise velocity' and position the Company as a compelling choice for clients, via differentiated capabilities, partnerships and sharper verticalization
- Client demand evidenced in delivered use cases — engineering productivity and build-cycle gains, ITSM cost reduction and automation-led transaction reduction at named client types (education services, travel & tourism, financial services)
- AI now accounts for 18% of the order book
- AI-led opportunities have scaled to represent 30% of the pipeline, highlighting strong adoption momentum
- AI opportunities are being actively pursued across 100+ clients

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margins accreted 70bps QoQ to 20.2% via utilization hike (91.8%), pyramid optimization, and price increases; offset partially by higher AI-led CSP bundle costs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position of Rs.31 Cr; Final dividend recommended at Rs.4.15/share; M&A on hold for immediate future, evaluating only unique tech opportunities in medium term.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed text discloses no plant, capacity or physical capex programme — Sonata's expansion is asset-light and platform/capability-led. In FY26 the Company launched AgentBridge, its cloud-agnostic Agentic AI platform for building and deploying next-generation Agentic AI solutions, and operationalized it internally with production-grade agents running for the HR and Finance teams. Capability build-out continued through Sonata University, which trained more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers in AI and delivered organisation-wide Vibe Code training, and through Program Edge, under which internal workflows — including immigration management and compensation and benefits administration — are being automated with an AI layer on top. Ecosystem expansion took the form of research partnerships with IISc (India) and the Wharton School (US) on Agentic AI, and of deeper hyperscaler alliances: Microsoft (continuing Inner Circle and Partner AI Council member, among the first recognised as a Microsoft Frontier Partner, Official Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner) and AWS (Premier Tier Services Partner, Gen AI Competency Partner), alongside Salesforce and Snowflake. Market expansion is being pursued by scaling the invest verticals HLS and BFSI, by deepening the North America business, and in India (SITL) by expanding the Microsoft channel into the SMC segment, broadening ISV partnerships beyond the three hyperscaler CSPs, and winning large System Integration deals that integrate Cisco, IBM, Dell and other ISV infrastructures with leading cloud platforms. The workforce stood at 6200+ Sonatians.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; disciplined execution; focused on continuity during leadership transition; confident in AI pipeline conversion despite macro headwinds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Proprietary Platformation™ framework underpinning its AI-first Modernization Engineering positioning
- Deep hyperscaler partnerships — Microsoft, AWS, Salesforce and Snowflake — used to deliver AI solutions to clients
- Microsoft standing: continuing member of the Microsoft Inner Circle and Partner AI Council, among the first companies recognised as a Microsoft Frontier Partner, and an Official Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner
- AWS standing: AWS Premier Tier Services Partner (highest level of recognition in the AWS Partner Network) and AWS Gen AI Competency Partner
- Owned Agentic AI platform AgentBridge, launched in FY26 and already running production-grade agents for the Company's own HR and Finance teams
- Research partnerships with IISc (India) and the Wharton School (US) on Agentic AI research and innovation
- AI-trained workforce — more than 92% of the workforce and 80% of managers trained in AI via Sonata University, with Vibe Code training rolled out organisation-wide
- Sticky client base with an aggregated Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) score of 4.3 out of 5 and 23 new customers added during the Financial Year
- Recognised employer brand (Jombay WOW Workplace 2025 in IT and ITES, Team Marksmen Most Preferred Workplace 2025-26, ET Now Best Organizations to Work 2025) supporting talent retention

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Elongated client decision cycles for AI projects; BFSI sector contraction pressures; Domestic channel policy changes by OEMs (Microsoft); Sustainability of TMT upturn.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: AI-led orders now 18% of total book indicating rapid product mix shift; Domestic business already recovered most of the OEM direct-billing loss within 4 quarters despite reported degrowth; 90% of workforce already AI-certified creating a latent margin lever if utilization dips.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Position Sonata as an AI-first Modernization Engineering company that helps enterprises transform from legacy systems to intelligent business platforms
- Embed AI across the organisation — client solutions, delivery and internal functions — and convert innovation into measurable business impact, shaping the path toward 'Sonata.AI'
- Drive platform-led transformation (Platformation.AI), agentic AI operating models and partner-led GTM acceleration (PLF-driven), moving clients from tool-based adoption to autonomous AI-driven execution at scale
- Build and scale proprietary AI platforms — Harmoni.AI, …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for legacy modernization and AI integration in BFSI/TMT amidst budget caution | Sonata Software Ltd | beneficiary | High | New CEO is primary architect of AI strategy; $280M pipeline provides visible runway; margin resilience proven at 20%+ even with flat revenue. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Two-business structure] The deck reports International Services and Domestic Business separately with radically different economics - the Domestic Business (SITL) shows Q1'27 revenue of 2505.6 INR crs against Gross Contribution of just 78.5 INR crs and EBITDA (Before Forex & OI) margin of 2.4%, consistent with its 'Grow Core Reselling/Platform' description; International Services shows Q1'27 revenue of 777.2 INR crs on a 15.4% EBITDA (Before Forex & OI) margin. Gross revenue of the reselling arm is not comparable to services revenue.
- [Client concentration] Revenue from Top 10 clients fell to 51.0% in Q1'27 from 54.0% in Q4'26 and 56% in Q1'26; Top 20 was 70.0% versus 69.0% in Q4'26. New customers added: 7 in Q1'27, same as Q4'26 and Q1'26.
- [Client-size cohorts] $5+ Mn clients numbered 12 in Q1'27 (13 in Q1'26), $3-5 Mn 9 (6), $1-3 Mn 32 (39) - the small-account cohort has been shrinking through the five quarters shown.
- [Geography mix] International Services revenue by geography at Q1'27: USA 71%, Europe 23%, ROW 6% - Europe has risen from 16.0% in Q1'26 while ROW fell from 10.0%.
- [Disclosure change] The covering letter describes the file as a 'revised Investors' Presentation for the quarter ended 30th June, 2026', i.e. a restatement of an earlier submission; the deck does not say what was revised.
